title: Three Mornings and One Short Pole
subtitle: 国家公民 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）
meta: 主题语境：国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）　|　核心词汇：flag　|　正文 348 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 flag 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the guard ① raised a flag that no officer in the square would have named, and he said the raising was the whole of the morning. The ② flag, meaning the banner itself and not the pole, ran three mornings and stayed unnamed in the book; a flag, he said, is the only thing in a square that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ flag in that square had the same short rope beside it, and the ④ flag at the far door, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A flag, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; the guard said the naming is the part that fills three mornings.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the flag was the whole of the matter, meaning the paving stone and not the banner. The ⑥ flag, meaning the paving stone and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody names; flag, he said, is either something you raise or the only word that means both a banner and a paving stone. He said the paving stone is the part they remember.

By 1978 the ⑦ flag had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short rope. The ⑧ flag of the whole thing, the guard wrote in September, was one square and three mornings of naming; flag, he said, is either the one at the far door or the reason you learned to name. He said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ flag I remember is the one named in the plan, which closed in 1980 and is still described as the quietest in the square. A ⑩ flag, my mother said in 1982, is the only one that improves by being named; every flag, she said, is a paving stone that has agreed to look like a banner. She said the paving stone was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 旗；旗帜（指广场上每一面旁边的那一面）
B. n. 旗帜（指那一面本身，与旗杆相对）
C. 固定搭配：raise a flag 升起一面旗帜
D. n. 旗帜（指留给孩子们的那一面）
E. n. 旗帜（抽象总称，指一处广场的升旗之事）
F. n. 旗帜（指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一面）
G. n. 石板；铺路石（flagstone，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 石板（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

items.q: raised a flag that no officer in the square would have named
The flag, meaning the banner itself and not the pole
the flag at the far door
the flag was the whole of the matter
The flag, meaning the paving stone
the flag had become a line in a plan
The flag of the whole thing
A flag, my mother said in 1982

answers.why: raise a flag 意为“升起一面旗帜”，1971 年那位卫兵升起了一面广场上没有一位军官肯说出名字的旗帜。
flag 意为“旗帜”，指那一面本身而不是旗杆，它经过了三个早晨而在簿子上没有被说出名字。
flag 意为“旗帜”，指广场上每一面旁边的那一面，每一面旁边都有同一根短短的绳索。
flag 意为“旗帜”，指留给孩子们的那一面，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
flag 意为“石板、铺路石”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说那块石板就是那件事的全部。
flag 意为“石板”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那一面旗帜，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
flag 意为“旗帜”，指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一面，到 1978 年这一面成了计划里的一行。
flag 意为“旗帜”，卫兵九月写道，整件事的升旗之事是一处广场和三个早晨的说出名字。
flag 意为“旗帜”，我记得的是计划里被说出名字的那一面，1980 年结束了，至今仍被说成广场上最安静的一面。
flag 为抽象总称，母亲 1982 年说，一面旗帜是唯一会因为被好好说出名字而变得更好的东西。
